\section[la noticia]{la noticia — the piece of news}

\label{lesson:ES-C495-noticia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to switch on, then the Spanish for to heat up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la noticia}
\textbf{la noticia} — \textquotedblleft{}the piece of news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tengo una buena noticia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have some good news.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Las noticias} on television are the news.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la noticia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la noticia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la noticia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to switch on, then the Spanish for to heat up, then say \emph{la noticia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la noticia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The piece of news\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ocurrir]{ocurrir — to happen}

\label{lesson:ES-C495-ocurrir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to heat up, then the Spanish for the piece of news.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ocurrir}
\textbf{ocurrir} — \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Qué ocurrió anoche?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{What happened last night?}
\end{quote}

A little more formal than \emph{pasar}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[suceder]{suceder — to happen, to take place}

\label{lesson:ES-C495-suceder}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the piece of news, then the Spanish for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: suceder}
\textbf{suceder} — \textquotedblleft{}to happen, to take place\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El accidente sucedió en la autopista.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The accident happened on the motorway.}
\end{quote}

News reports use it alongside \emph{ocurrir}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[desaparecer]{desaparecer — to disappear}

\label{lesson:ES-C495-desaparecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to happen, then the Spanish for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: desaparecer}
\textbf{desaparecer} — \textquotedblleft{}to disappear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Desapareció un perro en el parque.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A dog disappeared in the park.}
\end{quote}

It takes a \emph{z} in the first person present: \emph{desaparezco}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
